newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-GRAY LEADS AS SENIOR FIGHTS FOR OPEN PLACE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GRAY LEADS AS SENIOR FIGHTS FOR OPEN PLACE.

text.p: Australian Peter Senior, seeking a place in this year's British Open, was two shots off the pace after the first round of the New South Wales Challenge on Thursday.
Senior fired a four-under-par round of 68 to join compatriots Peter Lonard, Grant Kenny and Stuart Bouvier plus David Smail of New Zealand in third place.

Chris Gray, another Australian, grabbed the lead with an opening round of 66 to take a one-shot lead over compatriot Lucas Parsons, who started his round with five consecutive birdies, and Steve Alker of New Zealand.

Senior, the defending champion, needs to win the tournament to guarantee a place in the British Open at Royal Troon in July. The top three players on the Australasian PGA Tour Order of Merit will win exemptions for the Open.
A win this week would see Senior bump world number one Greg Norman out of third place on the Australasian Order of Merit, which is led by Australian Masters champion Lonard.
Australia's Brett Ogle was earlier told by tournament officials he could not use a "broomstick" style chipping iron with two grips on the shaft.
Ogle designed the club, made by joining two shafts on a regulation eight iron and used in the same pendulum style as a broomstick putter, in an attempt to overcome problems with his short game.

Australasian PGA director of operations Trevor Herden told Ogle he could not use the club because the game's governing body, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, stipulated that the putter was the only club which could have two grips.
Ogle later agreed to remove the second grip and carried the club in his golf bag but said after shooting a 73 that he had not used it.
